questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: What is Linux, strictly speaking?
questions.explanation: Linux names the kernel; distributions combine it with utilities, libraries, and applications.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: What does a Linux distribution generally provide?
options: Only the Linux kernel source code
The Linux kernel together with system software and package management
questions.explanation: A distribution packages the kernel with user-space tools, libraries, installers, and other software.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: During a custom Ubuntu server installation, what does partitioning determine?
options: Which users can log in over SSH
How disk space is divided into filesystems or partitions
questions.explanation: Partitioning allocates portions of storage for filesystems and related system uses.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which component is loaded early in a typical Linux startup sequence to initialize the system and start user space?
questions.explanation: The boot loader loads the kernel, which initializes hardware and starts the user-space init system.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: What is the general purpose of a run level or system target?
options: Select a system operating mode and associated services
questions.explanation: Run levels or targets describe system states, such as multi-user or rescue operation.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which command prints the current working directory?
questions.explanation: pwd prints the pathname of the current working directory.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: What does cd .. usually do?
questions.explanation: The path component .. refers to the parent directory.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which command lists directory entries, including hidden names with the usual option?
questions.explanation: ls -a includes names beginning with a dot, which ordinary ls may omit.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which command copies source.txt to backup.txt?
questions.explanation: cp copies a file; the source remains in place.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which command renames old.txt to new.txt in the same directory?
questions.explanation: mv moves a file and is commonly used to rename it.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which command prints a text file's contents to standard output?
questions.explanation: cat concatenates files to standard output; with one file it displays its contents.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which command displays the last lines of a log file?
questions.explanation: tail displays the end of a file; head displays its beginning.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which command searches file.txt for lines containing the word error?
questions.explanation: grep searches input lines for a matching pattern.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: What does sort names.txt normally do?
options: Prints the lines in sorted order
Compares two files byte by byte
questions.explanation: sort orders input lines and writes the result to standard output by default.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which command opens the manual page for grep?
questions.explanation: man followed by a command name requests that command's manual page.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which command searches a directory tree using criteria such as name and file type?
questions.explanation: find traverses a directory hierarchy and applies tests to discovered paths.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: What is a common distinction between locate and find?
options: locate commonly searches an indexed database; find searches directories directly
locate edits files; find only prints file contents
locate changes ownership; find changes permissions
There is no difference in their purpose
questions.explanation: locate is typically fast because it consults an index, which may not be current.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which command reports line-by-line differences between two text files?
questions.explanation: diff compares files and reports the changes needed to transform one into the other.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: What does file report about a pathname?
options: A description of the file type based on its contents
questions.explanation: file examines a pathname and reports a type description, often using content signatures.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which command creates a directory named reports?
questions.explanation: mkdir creates directories; rmdir removes an empty directory.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which command removes a file named draft.txt?
questions.explanation: rm removes file entries; rmdir is for empty directories.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: When does rmdir project usually succeed?
options: When project is an empty directory
Only when project is a regular file
questions.explanation: rmdir removes empty directories and normally refuses nonempty ones.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: What does touch report.txt do when report.txt does not exist?
questions.explanation: touch creates an empty file if needed and updates timestamps on an existing file.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: What is echo commonly used for in a shell?
questions.explanation: echo writes its arguments to standard output, often for messages or variable display.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which command prints the effective username of the current user?
questions.explanation: whoami prints the name associated with the current effective user ID.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which command can show users currently logged in?
questions.explanation: who reports information about users with current login sessions.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which command displays information about running processes?
questions.explanation: ps reports process status for selected processes or the current session.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: What does kill 2468 normally request?
options: Send the default termination signal to process ID 2468
questions.explanation: kill sends a signal to a process; the default signal is usually SIGTERM.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which command creates a symbolic link named shortcut pointing to target?
questions.explanation: ln -s creates a symbolic link whose stored target is the specified pathname.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: A hard link generally refers to what?
options: A text file containing a target pathname
Another directory entry for the same inode
A remote file on an FTP server
A compressed copy of a file
questions.explanation: Hard links are directory entries referring to the same inode on a filesystem.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which command decompresses a file compressed by gzip?
questions.explanation: gunzip decompresses gzip-format files; gzip -d is also commonly used.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which command extracts files from package.zip?
questions.explanation: unzip extracts members of a ZIP archive.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: Which tar option combination commonly creates an archive file?
questions.explanation: With tar, -c creates an archive and -f names the archive file.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: What is the usual purpose of a Makefile?
options: Describe build targets, dependencies, and commands for make
Define file permissions for every directory
questions.explanation: A Makefile describes targets and dependencies so make can run the needed build commands.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 1 Fundamentals and Commands
questions.question_text: In Bash, what does touch file{1..3} expand to before touch runs?
options: Three directories named file1 through file3
questions.explanation: Bash brace expansion produces the three separate words file1, file2, and file3.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: In a Unix permission string, which three classes are represented by rwx groups?
questions.explanation: The three permission classes are the owner, the file's group, and others.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: What permissions does chmod 640 report.txt set?
questions.explanation: 6 is rw-, 4 is r--, and 0 grants no permissions.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: What does chmod u+x script.sh do?
options: Adds execute permission for the file owner
Adds write permission for the group
questions.explanation: u selects the owner and +x adds execute permission for that class.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: On a directory, what does execute permission generally allow?
questions.explanation: Execute permission on a directory allows traversal when the pathname is known.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: Which command changes the owner of a file?
questions.explanation: chown changes file ownership; chgrp changes the group ownership.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: Which command changes a file's group ownership?
questions.explanation: chgrp assigns a different group as the file's group owner.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: What does an access control list add beyond the basic owner/group/others permission model?
options: Permissions for specified users or groups
questions.explanation: ACLs allow more specific per-user and per-group access entries.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: Which command displays ACL entries on a file?
questions.explanation: getfacl prints the access control list for a file or directory.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: Which command is used to modify ACL entries?
questions.explanation: setfacl adds, changes, or removes ACL entries.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: What is SSH primarily used for?
options: Secure remote login and command access
questions.explanation: SSH provides an encrypted protocol for remote login and related secure operations.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: SFTP is commonly used for what?
options: Secure file transfer over an SSH connection
questions.explanation: SFTP transfers and manages files using the SSH protocol for secure communication.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: Why are SSH and SFTP generally preferred to Telnet and traditional FTP for sensitive remote access?
options: They automatically give every user root access
They only work with text files
questions.explanation: Traditional Telnet and FTP do not protect credentials and data with encryption by default.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: What does mounting a filesystem do?
options: Makes a filesystem accessible at a directory in the current namespace
questions.explanation: Mounting attaches a filesystem to a directory called a mount point.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: Why should a mounted filesystem normally be unmounted before its device is disconnected?
options: To flush pending writes and detach it cleanly
To change its owner to root
To remove the mount-point directory automatically
questions.explanation: Unmounting helps ensure pending filesystem operations are completed before detaching storage.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: In vi or vim, which mode is used to type text into the buffer?
questions.explanation: Insert mode accepts typed text; normal mode is used for navigation and commands.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: Which vi key normally returns from Insert mode to Normal mode?
questions.explanation: Esc leaves Insert mode and returns to Normal mode in vi and vim.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: In vi Normal mode, what does pressing i usually do?
options: Enter Insert mode before the cursor
questions.explanation: i enters Insert mode before the current cursor position.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: What does the vi command :w save?
options: The current buffer to a file
questions.explanation: :w writes the current editing buffer to its file.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: Which vi command writes changes and then exits?
questions.explanation: :wq writes the buffer and quits the editor.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: What does :q! do in vi when there are unsaved changes?
options: Searches backward for an exclamation mark
questions.explanation: :q! forces quitting and discards unsaved buffer changes.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: In vi Normal mode, which command starts a forward search for a pattern?
questions.explanation: Typing / followed by a pattern starts a forward search in vi.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: In vi, what does :%s/old/new/g request?
options: Replace every occurrence of old with new throughout the file
Replace only the current word without confirmation
questions.explanation: % selects all lines and g replaces every matching occurrence on each selected line.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: In vi Normal mode, what does yy commonly do?
options: Yank or copy the current line
questions.explanation: yy copies the current line into vi's unnamed register.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: After copying a line in vi, which Normal-mode command commonly puts it below the current line?
questions.explanation: p puts the yanked text after the cursor or below the current line.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: In vi Normal mode, what does dd commonly do?
questions.explanation: dd deletes the current line and places it in the unnamed register.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: Which vi command displays line numbers?
questions.explanation: :set number enables displayed line numbers in vi or vim.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: Which setfacl entry grants user larry read, write, and execute access to a file?
questions.explanation: The ACL specification u:larry:rwx grants those permissions to the named user.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.subtopic: Denying a named user with ACL
questions.question_text: A file has an ACL entry granting a group read and write. How can an explicit named-user ACL prevent Moe from receiving permissions through that group entry?
options: Add Moe to the group a second time
Change the file name to include Moe
Add a user ACL entry for Moe with no permissions
Use chmod to grant Moe execute only
questions.explanation: A matching named-user ACL entry takes precedence over the group-class entries; an empty permission set denies Moe access, subject to ACL evaluation rules.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: A named-user ACL entry grants rwx, but the ACL mask is r--. What effective permissions can that user receive through that entry?
options: No permissions because a mask always denies access
questions.explanation: The ACL mask limits the effective permissions of named users, named groups, and the owning group class.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Session 2 File Management and Permissions
questions.question_text: In the syllabus lab, why is an ACL useful for the stooges group scenario?
options: It can grant group access while defining a separate named-user entry for Moe
It automatically creates the group and all users
It makes every file readable by all system users
It replaces the need for file ownership
questions.explanation: ACL entries can express group permissions and a more specific entry for an individual user.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What is the primary role of a command-line shell?
options: Interpret user commands and start programs
questions.explanation: A shell reads commands, interprets them, and launches programs or executes built-ins.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: Bash is an example of what?
questions.explanation: Bash is the Bourne Again Shell, a widely used command interpreter.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: Which assignment is valid in Bash?
questions.explanation: Bash variable assignment has no spaces around the equals sign.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: If name=Ravi, which expression expands to the variable's value in Bash?
questions.explanation: The dollar sign introduces parameter expansion, so $name yields the value of name.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What does export PATH usually do in Bash?
options: Marks PATH for inclusion in the environment of subsequently started programs
Changes PATH into a shell function
questions.explanation: export places a shell variable in the environment inherited by child processes.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: Which file is commonly used for interactive Bash settings for a user?
questions.explanation: .bashrc commonly contains settings for interactive non-login Bash shells.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: Which file is commonly read for user login-shell configuration on Bash systems?
questions.explanation: .bash_profile is a common Bash login startup file; other distributions may use .profile or .bash_login.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: In a shell script, what does $1 usually contain?
options: The exit status of the last command
questions.explanation: $1 expands to the first positional parameter supplied to the script or function.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What does $# expand to in a Bash script?
questions.explanation: $# gives the number of positional parameters.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: Which Bash command reads a line from standard input into variable answer?
questions.explanation: read assigns input fields from a line to the named shell variable.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: Which shell command commonly prints a message to standard output?
questions.explanation: echo writes its arguments to standard output.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: Which command correctly uses expr to add 4 and 5 in a traditional shell script?
questions.explanation: expr expects operands and operators as separate arguments; spaces are required around +.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What is the value of $((3 + 4 * 2)) in Bash?
questions.explanation: Multiplication has precedence over addition, so the arithmetic result is 3 + 8 = 11.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: In a shell filename pattern, what does * commonly match?
options: A directory separator and all later text
questions.explanation: The unquoted * wildcard matches any string of characters, including the empty string, within a pathname component.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: In a shell filename pattern, what does ? commonly match?
questions.explanation: The ? wildcard matches exactly one character in a pathname component.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: In Bash, what does test -f path check?
options: Whether path is a regular file
Whether path is readable by everyone
Whether path is a symbolic link only
questions.explanation: -f tests whether the pathname exists and refers to a regular file.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: Which test expression checks whether path is a directory?
questions.explanation: The -d file test is true when the pathname refers to a directory.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What does [ -r file ] test in a shell script?
options: Whether the file is a regular file
Whether the file is readable by the current process
Whether the file was recently modified
questions.explanation: -r checks whether the current process has read access to the pathname.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: In a shell test, what does [ -z value ] check?
options: Whether value is an empty string
questions.explanation: -z is true when its string argument has zero length.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: Which keyword closes a Bash if statement?
questions.explanation: Bash closes an if construct with fi.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: Which keyword closes a Bash case statement?
questions.explanation: case is terminated by esac, which is case spelled backward.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: When does a Bash while loop continue executing its body?
options: Only when its body contains break
questions.explanation: A while loop repeats while its condition list returns a successful status.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: When does a Bash until loop continue executing its body?
questions.explanation: An until loop repeats while its condition list fails and stops when it succeeds.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What does a Bash for loop commonly do with a list of words?
options: Runs its body once for each word
Runs only while a test is false
Creates a function for each word
questions.explanation: A for loop iterates through its word list, assigning each item to the loop variable in turn.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What does break do inside a shell loop?
questions.explanation: break terminates the current loop and continues after it.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What does continue do inside a shell loop?
options: Skips the remaining body for this iteration and proceeds to the next
questions.explanation: continue moves control to the next iteration of the nearest loop.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What does result=$(pwd) do in Bash?
options: Runs pwd and stores its standard output in result
questions.explanation: Command substitution captures a command's standard output for use in an assignment.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What is the usual effect of single quotes around $HOME in Bash?
options: They prevent variable expansion, so the literal characters $HOME are passed
They expand HOME and remove all spaces
They run the value as a command
questions.explanation: Single quotes preserve the literal characters inside them and suppress parameter expansion.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What does pushd commonly do?
options: Changes directory and saves the previous location on the directory stack
questions.explanation: pushd changes directories while maintaining a directory stack for later navigation.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What does popd commonly do?
options: Removes a directory-stack entry and changes to the resulting top directory
questions.explanation: popd removes an entry from the directory stack and typically changes to the new top.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What does the Bash history feature keep?
options: A copy of every file ever opened
A list of installed kernels only
A list of previously entered commands
questions.explanation: Bash history records commands entered in interactive sessions, subject to configuration.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What does appending & to a command commonly do in an interactive shell?
options: Starts it as a background job
Redirects its output to a file named ampersand
questions.explanation: A trailing & asks the shell to start the command asynchronously in the background.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: Which shell command lists the current shell's jobs?
questions.explanation: jobs displays jobs known to the current interactive shell.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What does fg do for a suspended or background job known to the shell?
options: Brings the job to the foreground
questions.explanation: fg resumes or continues a shell job in the foreground.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: Which statement describes a shell built-in?
options: It must always be stored in /usr/bin
It can only run on a cloud virtual machine
It is a file permission bit
The shell implements it directly rather than launching a separate executable
questions.explanation: Built-ins such as cd are implemented by the shell process itself.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What is a shell function useful for?
options: Grouping reusable shell commands under a name
Changing the Linux kernel without rebooting
questions.explanation: A function packages commands so they can be invoked by name within a shell.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: Inside a Bash function, what does $1 usually refer to?
options: The first argument passed to the function
questions.explanation: A function receives positional parameters; $1 refers to its first argument while it runs.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What is tput commonly used for in shell scripts?
questions.explanation: tput accesses terminal capabilities, such as cursor movement or text attributes.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What does the pipe character | do between two shell commands?
options: Runs the second command only as root
Connects the first command's standard output to the second command's standard input
questions.explanation: A pipeline passes standard output from a command to standard input of the next.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What does command < input.txt do?
options: Uses input.txt as the command's standard input
Appends a command to the file
Searches the file for a command
questions.explanation: The < redirection operator opens the named file as standard input.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What does command > output.txt normally do?
options: Appends standard output without changing existing content
Redirects standard output to output.txt, truncating it first if it exists
Sends errors only to the terminal
questions.explanation: > redirects standard output and creates or truncates the target file.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: If files contains a space-separated string, what does quoting its expansion usually preserve that an unquoted expansion may not?
options: The value as separate arguments for every character
The value as a shell comment
The expanded value as one argument, including its spaces
The value as a command substitution
questions.explanation: Quoting a variable expansion prevents word splitting and pathname expansion on its value.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What must generally be true to execute a shell script directly as ./script.sh?
options: It must be owned by root
It has execute permission and a valid interpreter line or executable format
questions.explanation: Direct execution requires execute permission and a recognized executable format, commonly with a shebang.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: Which Bash startup file is commonly run when a login shell exits?
questions.explanation: .bash_logout may contain commands executed when a Bash login shell exits.

questions.topic: Linux Programming: Sessions 3–4 Shell Programming
questions.question_text: What is the intended effect of assigning /sbin/nologin as a user's login shell?
options: Grant the user unrestricted root access
Prevent a normal interactive login session for that account
Make the account a system service
questions.explanation: nologin refuses interactive login sessions, commonly for accounts that should not receive a shell.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of a version control system?
options: Track changes to files over time and support collaboration
questions.explanation: Version control records changes and helps users compare, restore, and collaborate on project history.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: Which command initializes a Git repository in the current directory?
questions.explanation: git init creates Git repository metadata in the current directory.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: Which command shows changed, staged, and untracked files in a repository?
questions.explanation: git status summarizes the working tree and staging area.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: What does git add report.csv normally do?
options: Stages the file's current changes for the next commit
Deletes the file from the working tree
questions.explanation: git add places selected changes in the staging area.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: What does a Git commit record?
options: A copy of the remote website
A snapshot of staged repository changes with metadata
questions.explanation: A commit records the staged project snapshot along with author, time, and message metadata.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: Which command creates a commit with the message 'Add analysis'?
questions.explanation: git commit -m supplies the commit message on the command line.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: Which command displays the repository's commit history?
questions.explanation: git log displays commit history, commonly starting with the most recent commit.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: Which command compares unstaged working-tree changes with the index?
questions.explanation: git diff without extra options shows unstaged differences between the working tree and index.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: Why create a Git branch for a new feature?
options: To duplicate the entire operating system
To develop changes separately from another branch until they are ready
To upload files without a remote
questions.explanation: A branch provides an independent line of development that can later be merged.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: Which command lists local branches in a Git repository?
questions.explanation: git branch with no arguments lists local branches.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: Which modern Git command switches to an existing branch named feature?
questions.explanation: git switch changes the current branch to an existing branch.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: Which command creates a new branch named testing and switches to it?
questions.explanation: git switch -c creates a branch and checks it out in one operation.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: What does git merge feature do when run on the target branch?
options: Creates a GitHub account named feature
Integrates changes from feature into the current branch
questions.explanation: git merge combines the changes from the named branch into the current branch.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: What is a merge conflict?
options: A conflict between two remote URLs regardless of content
A case where Git cannot automatically reconcile competing changes
questions.explanation: A conflict occurs when Git needs a person to decide how overlapping changes should be combined.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: After editing a file to resolve a merge conflict, what is normally needed before committing the resolution?
questions.explanation: The resolved file must be staged so the resolution can be recorded in a commit.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: What is a Git remote?
options: A named reference to another repository, often hosted online
A branch that cannot be checked out
questions.explanation: A remote stores the location and name of another repository for fetch and push operations.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: What does git push commonly do?
options: Downloads a repository for the first time
Sends local commits to a configured remote repository
questions.explanation: git push publishes local commits to a remote branch.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: Which command copies a remote Git repository into a new local directory?
questions.explanation: git clone downloads repository data and checks out an initial working copy.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: What is GitHub in the context of the syllabus?
options: A hosting and collaboration service for Git repositories
questions.explanation: GitHub hosts Git repositories and adds collaboration features such as reviews and issue tracking.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: A developer has made local commits and wants to publish them to GitHub. Which step is normally used?
options: Run git diff until it uploads
Configure a remote if needed, then push the branch
Use git status to publish commits
questions.explanation: The local repository needs a remote destination, and git push transfers commits to it.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: Git status reports a file as untracked. What does this mean?
options: The file has already been committed
The file is stored on GitHub only
Git is not currently tracking that file in the repository index
The file is a merge conflict
questions.explanation: An untracked file exists in the working tree but has not been added to version control.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: What is the Git staging area used for?
options: Selecting changes to include in the next commit
questions.explanation: The index or staging area lets a user choose changes for the next commit.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: What information is needed by git clone to copy a GitHub repository?
questions.explanation: git clone uses a repository URL or other repository location.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: After completing and committing a feature branch, what operation commonly integrates it into the main development branch?
options: Run git init inside every source file
Merge the feature branch into the target branch
Use chmod on the branch name
questions.explanation: Merging integrates a completed line of development into the chosen target branch.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 1 Git and GitHub Fundamentals
questions.question_text: Which Git command is useful for comparing two commits or branches?
questions.explanation: git diff can compare working-tree changes, commits, and branch tips.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: Which description best captures cloud computing?
options: A single desktop computer disconnected from a network
A programming language for virtual machines
A backup copy stored only on a USB drive
On-demand network access to shared configurable computing resources
questions.explanation: Cloud computing provides network-accessible resources that can be provisioned and released on demand.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: Which cloud characteristic lets a user provision resources without human interaction with each provider?
questions.explanation: On-demand self-service allows consumers to provision capabilities as needed through self-service interfaces.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: Broad network access means cloud capabilities are generally available through what?
options: Network mechanisms accessible from varied client devices
A dedicated cable connected to one user's keyboard
questions.explanation: Cloud services are reachable over networks using standard mechanisms and varied client platforms.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: What does resource pooling describe in cloud computing?
options: Each consumer must own a separate datacenter
All resources are permanently assigned to one user
Provider resources serve multiple consumers using a shared, dynamically allocated pool
Users pool their passwords in a shared file
questions.explanation: Resource pooling allows provider resources to serve multiple consumers with dynamic allocation.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: What is rapid elasticity in a cloud context?
options: Every resource is fixed for the life of the account
A virtual machine can only run one process
Resources can scale out or in quickly with demand
questions.explanation: Rapid elasticity describes quickly increasing or decreasing available resources as needed.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: What does measured service commonly enable?
options: Monitoring and metering resource use for transparency or billing
Unlimited free compute for every account
Manual installation of every operating system
questions.explanation: Measured service tracks resource use so provider and consumer can monitor consumption.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: Which is a common benefit of cloud computing?
options: Provisioning capacity without purchasing all physical hardware in advance
questions.explanation: Cloud services can reduce upfront infrastructure acquisition and speed provisioning.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: Which is a realistic cloud adoption consideration?
options: Every cloud workload has identical costs
Dependence on network connectivity and provider service availability
questions.explanation: Cloud workloads can depend on network access and provider availability, among other considerations.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: Which set contains the three cloud vendors named in the syllabus?
questions.explanation: The syllabus names Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: Which item is a typical cloud computing component or resource?
options: Compute, storage, or networking capacity delivered as a service
questions.explanation: Cloud environments provide resources such as compute, storage, and networking.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: A public cloud service is generally operated by whom?
options: One private household for its own laptop
A provider offering services to multiple customers
questions.explanation: Public cloud infrastructure is offered by a provider for use by multiple customers.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: What is a defining characteristic of a private cloud?
options: It must be hosted on a personal phone
Cloud infrastructure is dedicated to a single organization
It is always operated by AWS
questions.explanation: A private cloud is used exclusively by one organization, though it may be hosted internally or externally.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: What does a hybrid cloud combine?
options: A database table and a spreadsheet only
Two programming languages in one file
Distinct cloud environments, such as private and public clouds, connected for coordinated use
questions.explanation: A hybrid cloud connects distinct cloud environments that remain separate but can support coordinated workloads.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: When comparing AWS, Azure, and GCP for a workload, what is a sound first step?
options: Compare required services, regions, pricing, integrations, and operational needs
Assume every service has identical behavior and price
Ignore data location and compliance requirements
questions.explanation: Vendor selection should consider workload requirements and the specific service capabilities and constraints.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: What does cloud paradigm refer to in this course context?
options: A type of Linux file permission
Different ways of organizing and delivering computing resources as cloud services
questions.explanation: Cloud paradigms describe models for organizing, deploying, and consuming cloud resources.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: An analytics team starts temporary compute resources through a portal without waiting for provider staff. Which cloud characteristic is illustrated?
questions.explanation: The team provisions resources itself when needed, illustrating on-demand self-service.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: A web service adds instances during a traffic spike and removes them when demand falls. Which cloud property is most directly shown?
questions.explanation: Scaling capacity up and down with changing demand demonstrates elasticity.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: A provider reports the storage and compute consumed by each account for billing. Which characteristic supports this?
questions.explanation: Measured service monitors and reports resource usage.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: Multiple customers draw capacity from a provider's shared infrastructure while remaining logically isolated. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: Resource pooling shares provider capacity across consumers while logical controls separate their workloads.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: A user accesses a cloud dashboard from a laptop and a phone over a network. Which characteristic does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: Broad network access supports access through networks from varied client devices.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: A startup needs more compute capacity next week but cannot buy servers in time. Which cloud benefit is most relevant?
questions.explanation: Cloud resources can often be provisioned faster than purchasing and installing physical hardware.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: A service outage at a cloud provider prevents customers from reaching a hosted application. What concern does this illustrate?
options: The need for shell brace expansion
questions.explanation: Cloud consumers depend on the provider's service availability and their own connectivity.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: Which vendor operates Azure?
questions.explanation: Azure is Microsoft's cloud platform.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: Which vendor operates Google Cloud Platform?
questions.explanation: Google Cloud Platform is operated by Google.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 2 Introduction to Cloud Computing
questions.question_text: Which vendor operates Amazon Web Services?
questions.explanation: Amazon Web Services is Amazon's cloud platform.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: What does Software as a Service (SaaS) provide to a consumer?
options: A provider-managed application accessed as a service
A hypervisor for installing an operating system
questions.explanation: SaaS delivers a complete application that the provider operates for consumers.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: Which resources are most associated with Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)?
questions.explanation: IaaS provides fundamental infrastructure resources such as compute, storage, and networking.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: What does Platform as a Service (PaaS) primarily provide?
options: A managed platform for building and deploying applications
questions.explanation: PaaS supplies managed application development or runtime capabilities on underlying infrastructure.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: A company wants to deploy its application code without managing virtual machines or the operating system. Which model is the closest fit?
questions.explanation: PaaS generally abstracts infrastructure and operating-system management while providing an application platform.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: A team needs control over its virtual machine operating system and installed software. Which model generally offers that level of control?
questions.explanation: IaaS consumers typically manage the guest operating system and applications on provisioned infrastructure.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: An organization subscribes to a browser-based customer relationship management application operated by its vendor. Which model is this?
questions.explanation: The customer consumes a complete vendor-managed application, which is SaaS.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: Compared with traditional packaged software installed and maintained locally, SaaS is commonly accessed how?
options: As a provider-hosted application over a network
By compiling the provider's source code
questions.explanation: SaaS is generally delivered as a network-accessible application managed by the service provider.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: Which is a potential benefit of SaaS for an organization?
options: Complete control of the provider's physical servers
No need to manage user access
Less need to install and maintain the application on each local machine
questions.explanation: Provider-hosted SaaS can reduce local installation and application-maintenance work.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: Which can be a limitation or trade-off when using SaaS?
options: Less control over the provider's application infrastructure and update schedule
The customer must buy a hypervisor for every browser
The service cannot be accessed from a network
Every SaaS application requires source-code compilation by the customer
questions.explanation: The provider manages the application, which can limit the consumer's control over infrastructure and release timing.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: In a typical IaaS arrangement, who is responsible for configuring applications installed inside the customer's virtual machine?
questions.explanation: The IaaS customer normally manages guest operating systems and applications, while the provider manages underlying infrastructure.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: What does virtualization allow a physical computer to do?
options: Turn every file into a cloud service
Remove the need for an operating system
Run isolated virtual computing environments using shared hardware
Guarantee that no application can fail
questions.explanation: Virtualization abstracts hardware resources so multiple isolated virtual machines can use one physical host.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: What is the role of a hypervisor?
options: Replace a guest operating system's applications
Create and manage virtual machines on host hardware
questions.explanation: A hypervisor allocates host resources to virtual machines and manages their execution.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: Where does a Type 1 hypervisor generally run?
options: As an ordinary application inside a guest browser
On top of a spreadsheet program
questions.explanation: A Type 1 or bare-metal hypervisor runs directly on host hardware.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: A desktop virtualization program runs as an application on a host operating system. What type is it commonly classified as?
questions.explanation: A Type 2 hypervisor runs on top of a conventional host operating system.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: What does provisioning a virtual machine generally involve?
options: Selecting resources and creating a configured VM for use
Writing a SaaS user manual only
questions.explanation: Provisioning creates and configures a VM with selected compute, storage, network, and image settings.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: What is virtual machine migration?
options: Converting a VM into a Git branch
Moving a VM or its workload from one host or location to another
questions.explanation: Migration transfers a VM or workload between hosts or environments, sometimes with limited downtime.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: What is the goal of live VM migration?
options: Move a running VM with little or no service interruption
Erase the VM's memory before copying it
Convert SaaS into a physical package
Stop all cloud network traffic permanently
questions.explanation: Live migration aims to move a running VM while minimizing downtime.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: An organization deploys cloud infrastructure for exclusive use by itself. Which deployment model is this?
questions.explanation: A private cloud is dedicated to one organization.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: What is vendor lock-in in a cloud environment?
options: A hypervisor refusing to start a VM once
A file permission that prevents reading
Difficulty moving workloads because they depend on provider-specific services or formats
A Git branch that cannot be merged
questions.explanation: Provider-specific dependencies can make migration to another platform costly or complex.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: Which factor can complicate moving sensitive workloads to a cloud provider?
options: The ability to create a Git commit
The use of a for loop
Data governance, security, or compliance requirements
questions.explanation: Organizations must address security, privacy, governance, and compliance for hosted data and systems.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: What is a web service generally designed to expose?
options: Functionality or data that other software can access over a network
A virtual machine's physical power supply
questions.explanation: A web service makes software functionality or data available to clients through network interfaces.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: A small team wants to use a finished email and calendar application without managing servers. Which model is the best match?
questions.explanation: The team wants a complete application, which fits Software as a Service.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: A developer wants a managed runtime and deployment platform but still supplies application code. Which model is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: PaaS provides the application platform while the developer supplies and manages application code.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: An administrator needs to choose the guest OS and configure system packages on a cloud VM. Which model is a likely fit?
questions.explanation: IaaS provides the VM-level control needed to configure a guest operating system.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: Which sequence generally moves from most consumer control over infrastructure to least?
questions.explanation: Consumers usually manage more in IaaS, less in PaaS, and least of the application stack in SaaS.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: Why might an organization use virtualization in a private cloud?
options: To allocate shared physical resources to isolated virtual machines
To replace all network protocols with shell commands
questions.explanation: Virtualization supports resource sharing and isolation for workloads on private infrastructure.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: Which operational task is more commonly handled by the customer with traditional packaged software than with SaaS?
options: Providing the internet service for the software vendor
Installing and maintaining the local application deployment
questions.explanation: Packaged software is commonly installed and maintained by the organization using it.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: What is one purpose of keeping workloads in separate virtual machines on the same host?
options: Make all VMs share one user password
Ensure each VM uses a different cloud vendor
Avoid the need for physical processors
Provide logical isolation between operating-system environments
questions.explanation: VM boundaries provide separate guest environments and help isolate workloads.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: What is a VM image commonly used for?
options: Providing a template from which virtual machines can be launched
questions.explanation: An image contains a prepared operating-system and software configuration used to create VMs.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: Which item is an example of a virtualization type or use named in cloud computing study?
questions.explanation: Server virtualization is a common type of virtualization used to run multiple VMs on hosts.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: Which is a likely advantage of IaaS over buying and operating physical servers?
options: The customer never manages any software
The operating system is chosen by the web browser
Infrastructure capacity can be provisioned as needed
Network connectivity is no longer required
questions.explanation: IaaS can make infrastructure capacity available without the customer buying each physical server.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: A PaaS application depends on a provider-specific runtime. What trade-off might this create?
options: The application no longer needs source code
The service can no longer be network-accessible
Portability to another provider may become harder
questions.explanation: Provider-specific runtimes and services can create portability challenges or vendor lock-in.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: Which is the clearest example of SaaS?
options: A hosted document-editing application used through a browser
questions.explanation: A provider-hosted application used through a browser is a typical SaaS offering.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: Which statement about a private cloud is accurate?
options: It must be accessible to every public user
It is dedicated for use by one organization, regardless of whether it is internally or externally hosted
It is the same as SaaS
questions.explanation: Private cloud describes exclusive organizational use, not necessarily who owns or hosts the hardware.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 3–4 Service Models and Virtualization
questions.question_text: Before migrating a VM to another host, which compatibility concern is important?
options: Whether the source directory has a .bashrc file
Whether the Git commit message is under 50 characters
Whether the destination supports the VM's requirements and resources
Whether a SaaS user can change their password
questions.explanation: Migration requires destination compatibility for the VM's configuration, storage, networking, and resources.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: Why should deployed cloud services be monitored?
options: To remove the need for backups
To make every VM publicly accessible
To observe health, performance, availability, and resource use
questions.explanation: Monitoring provides visibility into service health and consumption so issues can be detected and managed.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: A cloud workload's CPU usage stays high and response time worsens. What is a sensible administrative response?
options: Inspect monitoring data and determine whether capacity or application tuning is needed
Assume the provider will fix application code
questions.explanation: Monitoring data can help identify whether the issue requires scaling, tuning, or troubleshooting.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: What is a first necessary step before deploying an application to a cloud service?
options: Identify the application's runtime, configuration, and resource requirements
Turn every service into a public endpoint
questions.explanation: Deployment planning begins by understanding what the application needs to run correctly.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: A team needs virtual CPU and memory to run a Linux application. Which broad cloud product category should it evaluate?
questions.explanation: Compute products provide processing capacity, commonly through VMs, containers, or functions.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: When comparing cloud products for an application, which factors are most useful?
options: The number of letters in its name
Whether it shares a color with the source code
Required capabilities, cost, performance, and operational responsibilities
questions.explanation: A useful comparison considers workload needs, costs, performance, and who operates each layer.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: What is the purpose of a monitoring alert?
options: Notify operators when a defined condition or threshold is met
Replace the need to collect metrics
Make a service private by default
questions.explanation: Alerts draw attention to conditions that may require investigation or action.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: Which cloud benefit can help a project with unpredictable demand?
options: A permanent guarantee that no capacity limit exists
Adjustable capacity that can scale with workload needs
questions.explanation: Cloud capacity can often be adjusted more flexibly than fixed on-premises capacity.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: Why should teams monitor cloud spending as well as performance?
options: Monitoring is required to create a Git repository
Cloud services never charge by usage
Usage-based services can incur costs as resources are consumed
Performance metrics automatically change service prices
questions.explanation: Metered or provisioned resources may accrue charges, so usage and cost should be observed.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: A cloud deployment succeeds, but users cannot reach the application because its network access is not configured. What area should be checked?
questions.explanation: A deployed application also needs suitable network paths and access configuration.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: Which workload is most directly suited to a cloud compute service?
options: Running application code that needs CPU and memory
questions.explanation: Compute services provide processing resources for running applications and workloads.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: A web application needs persistent files that are not tied to one VM's local disk. Which product category should be considered?
questions.explanation: Cloud storage services can provide persistent data storage separately from a VM's local disk.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: Two providers offer similar compute services. What should the team compare before choosing?
options: The spelling of the providers' names
Pricing, regions, features, scaling, and support requirements
questions.explanation: Service selection should be based on functional, operational, geographic, and cost requirements.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: After deploying an application, what should the team do next to confirm it is operating correctly?
options: Test the endpoint and monitor service health
questions.explanation: Testing and monitoring verify that the deployment is reachable and behaving as expected.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: A business needs predictable operation during a provider outage. Which planning approach is relevant?
options: Assess availability requirements and design recovery or redundancy accordingly
Assume every provider outage is impossible
questions.explanation: Availability needs should inform redundancy, backup, and recovery planning.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: A team wants a managed function that runs in response to events rather than maintaining a long-running VM. Which compute approach should it evaluate?
questions.explanation: Event-triggered functions provide compute without requiring the team to manage a persistent server instance.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: Why might a team use a cloud service instead of purchasing physical infrastructure for a short-lived experiment?
options: It can provision and release capacity without long-term hardware ownership
questions.explanation: Temporary cloud resources can be provisioned for an experiment and released when no longer needed.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: Which service model gives the consumer a complete application while the provider manages the platform and infrastructure?
questions.explanation: SaaS delivers an application as a service with provider-managed underlying layers.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: Why does deploying an application to the cloud still require customer configuration?
options: The customer must configure workload-specific settings, access, and application behavior
The provider cannot supply any compute resources
Cloud services do not use networks
The application source code is always deleted
questions.explanation: Cloud providers supply services, but customers still configure and operate workload-specific components according to the model.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: What can service monitoring help an administrator identify?
options: The meaning of every source-code variable
Capacity bottlenecks, errors, and availability issues
questions.explanation: Monitoring signals help detect failures, performance degradation, and capacity issues.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: Which statement about cloud benefits is most accurate?
options: Cloud guarantees every workload is cheaper
Cloud removes every need for system administration
Cloud can improve provisioning flexibility, but costs and operational risks still need management
questions.explanation: Cloud can provide flexibility, but cost, reliability, security, and operational responsibilities still matter.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: What does cloud architecture describe?
options: How cloud components and services are organized to deliver a system
questions.explanation: Cloud architecture describes system components, their relationships, and how they meet workload needs.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: What does scalability mean for a cloud application?
options: The ability to handle increased or decreased workload by adjusting resources or design
The guarantee that code has no bugs
The ability to run without storage
The process of changing a user's password
questions.explanation: Scalability is the capacity to accommodate workload changes by adjusting resources or architecture.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: What does availability describe?
options: How many lines of code a service contains
Whether a service is accessible and usable when needed
How quickly a branch can be renamed
questions.explanation: Availability concerns the proportion of time a service is operational and accessible.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: What is fault tolerance?
options: Preventing every possible failure from occurring
Continuing to provide service despite some component failures
questions.explanation: Fault-tolerant designs continue functioning when some components fail.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: What is a common purpose of a multi-tier architecture?
options: Place all code and data in a single file
Replace the database with a load balancer
Separate responsibilities such as presentation, application logic, and data storage
questions.explanation: Separating tiers makes components easier to manage, scale, and secure independently.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: What does a load balancer do?
options: Distributes incoming requests across multiple backend instances
Stores application source code in Git
questions.explanation: A load balancer distributes traffic among backend targets to improve utilization and availability.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: What is the purpose of auto-scaling?
options: Adjust the number or size of resources according to configured demand or conditions
questions.explanation: Auto-scaling changes capacity based on policies, metrics, schedules, or demand.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: How can caching improve a cloud application?
options: Guarantee that all data is always current without invalidation
Reuse frequently requested data to reduce repeated work or latency
questions.explanation: Caches can reduce repeated computation or data access, though freshness and invalidation must be considered.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: What characterizes a monolithic application architecture?
options: Every feature must run in a separate cloud provider
Major application functions are packaged and deployed as one unit
questions.explanation: A monolith is commonly built and deployed as one application unit.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: What is a common characteristic of microservices architecture?
options: Application capabilities are divided into smaller services that communicate through interfaces
The entire system must be one executable
Every service runs only on a laptop
questions.explanation: Microservices structure an application as smaller services with defined communication interfaces.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: What does serverless computing mean from the developer's perspective?
options: The provider manages much of the server infrastructure while code runs on demand
Every function must run on a local workstation
questions.explanation: Serverless abstracts server management from the developer; provider infrastructure still runs the code.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: Which architecture is commonly suited to short, event-triggered tasks with provider-managed execution infrastructure?
options: A manually maintained physical server only
questions.explanation: Serverless functions are commonly invoked by events and reduce direct server management.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: What is a potential cost of splitting a monolith into many microservices?
options: More network communication and operational coordination to manage
questions.explanation: Microservices can improve independent deployment but add coordination, networking, and observability complexity.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: What does the shared responsibility model explain?
options: How security and operational responsibilities are divided between provider and customer
How cloud bills are split among employees
How a VM's memory is divided among programs
questions.explanation: The model clarifies which security and operational tasks belong to the provider and which remain with the customer.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: In a typical IaaS environment, who is generally responsible for configuring user access inside the guest operating system?
questions.explanation: In IaaS, customers commonly manage guest operating systems, identities, and application-level configuration.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: Why deploy redundant instances across separate failure domains?
options: To make all requests use one server
To reduce the chance that one localized failure stops the whole service
questions.explanation: Redundancy across failure domains can improve availability when one component or location fails.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: A system has several application servers but only one unreplicated database. What architectural concern remains?
options: The service has too many load balancers
The system cannot use a cache
The database may be a single point of failure
questions.explanation: A sole database can become a single point of failure even when other tiers are redundant.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: Adding more application instances behind a load balancer is an example of which scaling direction?
questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling adds instances; vertical scaling increases resources on an individual instance.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: How can a load balancer's health checks support availability?
options: Increase the password length on every VM
Avoid sending requests to instances that are reported unhealthy
Delete cached data on every request
questions.explanation: Health checks allow a load balancer to route around targets that are not responding properly.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: What must a design consider when cached data can change frequently?
options: How to prevent all users from accessing the application
Whether the cache can replace the source code
How and when cached entries are refreshed or invalidated
How to disable every database update
questions.explanation: Cache invalidation or expiration policies help balance performance with data freshness.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
