questions.question_text: In a multi-tier application, why might the database tier be kept inaccessible from the public internet?
options: To make the database run without storage
To prevent the application tier from connecting
To increase the number of public endpoints
To reduce direct exposure and allow access only through intended application components
questions.explanation: Restricting database access reduces attack surface and enforces intended network paths.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: A single application instance reaches its capacity during peak traffic. Which design pattern can distribute requests across additional instances?
questions.explanation: A load balancer distributes requests across multiple application instances.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: Which signal could an auto-scaling policy use to decide whether more instances are needed?
options: The color of the deployment dashboard
A configured workload metric such as CPU utilization or request count
The length of the project name
The number of comments in source files
questions.explanation: Auto-scaling policies can use metrics that reflect workload demand or resource pressure.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: A small application has simple requirements and one team. What is a reasonable architecture decision principle?
options: Always use the maximum number of microservices
Always use serverless regardless of workload
Choose the simplest architecture that meets current needs and can evolve
Choose a design without considering operational skills
questions.explanation: Architecture should fit workload and team needs; unnecessary complexity adds operational cost.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 7 Cloud Architecture
questions.question_text: Which design best reduces dependence on one application server?
options: Store all requests on one local desktop
Place every component on one unreplicated VM
Run multiple instances and route traffic around unhealthy instances
questions.explanation: Multiple instances with health-aware routing reduce dependence on any single application server.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: What is Amazon EC2 primarily used to provide?
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 provides virtual server instances that can run workloads in AWS.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: When launching a Linux EC2 instance, what does an AMI provide?
options: A template containing the operating system and configuration used to start the instance
questions.explanation: An Amazon Machine Image provides a launch template, including an operating-system image and configuration.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: Which protocol is commonly used to securely access a Linux VM remotely?
questions.explanation: SSH is commonly used for encrypted command-line access to Linux servers.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: Which protocol is commonly used for interactive remote desktop access to a Windows Server VM?
questions.explanation: Remote Desktop Protocol is commonly used to access a Windows graphical desktop remotely.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: What does an AWS VPC provide?
options: A logically isolated virtual network for AWS resources
questions.explanation: A VPC is a logically isolated network in which AWS resources can be launched.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: What is an EC2 key pair commonly used for when connecting to a Linux instance?
options: Public-key authentication for secure SSH access
questions.explanation: A key pair supports public-key authentication when connecting to an instance, subject to its configuration.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: What is an EC2 security group used for?
options: Control inbound and outbound network traffic for associated resources
questions.explanation: Security groups act as stateful virtual firewalls controlling traffic to and from associated resources.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: What is a subnet within a VPC?
options: A Git branch stored on EC2
A range of IP addresses within the VPC network
questions.explanation: A subnet divides a VPC address range into a smaller network segment.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: What does a VPC route table determine?
options: Where network traffic from a subnet is directed
Which user can edit a Git commit
How many files fit in an S3 bucket
questions.explanation: Route tables contain rules that direct network traffic to destinations.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: What is the purpose of attaching an internet gateway to a VPC?
options: Provide a path for communication between the VPC and the internet when routing and security allow it
questions.explanation: An internet gateway enables internet connectivity for VPC resources when routes and access rules are configured.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: What type of storage service is Amazon S3?
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 is an object storage service for storing and retrieving data objects.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: In S3, where are objects stored?
questions.explanation: S3 objects are stored in buckets, which provide a namespace and organizational container.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: What does AWS Lambda provide?
options: Managed serverless execution for functions in response to events or requests
A block device attached to every VM
questions.explanation: Lambda runs code in a managed environment without requiring the customer to manage a persistent server.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: What can cause an AWS Lambda function to run?
options: A vi editor line number only
A configured event or request source
A Linux file permission change on any computer
A Git branch name by itself
questions.explanation: Lambda functions are invoked by configured event sources or direct requests.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: What does an EC2 instance type generally describe?
options: A combination of compute, memory, storage, and networking capacity
questions.explanation: Instance types define hardware resource profiles for virtual machines.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: A Linux EC2 instance is running, but SSH access times out. Which configuration should be checked first alongside network reachability?
options: Whether the S3 bucket has a website name
Whether a Docker image was pushed
Whether the Git commit has a tag
Whether the security group permits inbound SSH from the intended source
questions.explanation: SSH requires an allowed network path, including appropriate inbound rules and routing.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: A Windows Server VM needs remote graphical access. Which combination is most relevant?
options: RDP access and network rules that permit the connection
Git merge and a Lambda layer
A Linux shell and tar archive
questions.explanation: Windows remote desktop access commonly uses RDP, and network controls must permit it.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: What is a typical effect of stopping an EC2 instance?
options: The VM is powered off and can generally be started again later
questions.explanation: Stopping powers off an instance while allowing it to be started again, subject to instance and storage behavior.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: What is a typical effect of terminating an EC2 instance?
options: The instance merely enters a paused state
The VPC changes to a public cloud
The instance is permanently removed from the running inventory
The instance becomes a Lambda function
questions.explanation: Termination ends the instance; deletion behavior for attached storage depends on its settings.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: A team stores application code in GitHub and wants to deploy it to an EC2 Linux VM. What is the role of Git in this workflow?
options: Track and retrieve application source code for deployment
questions.explanation: Git tracks the source code and can be used to clone or update it on the deployment environment.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: Why create a VPC for an AWS application?
options: To define an isolated network environment for its cloud resources
questions.explanation: A VPC provides network boundaries and configuration for resources belonging to a workload.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: Which data is a natural fit for Amazon S3 object storage?
options: Images, backups, or other files stored as objects
questions.explanation: S3 is suited to durable storage and retrieval of file-like objects such as images and backups.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: What is Microsoft Azure?
questions.explanation: Azure is Microsoft's cloud platform, offering compute, storage, data, and other services.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: What does Azure Storage provide?
options: Cloud storage services for application data
questions.explanation: Azure Storage is a family of cloud storage services for different data needs.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: What does Azure Functions provide?
questions.explanation: Azure Functions runs code in response to triggers without requiring direct server management.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: What is the purpose of Azure data services in an application architecture?
options: Provide managed capabilities for storing, processing, or analyzing data
Control a Linux editor's search mode
questions.explanation: Azure data services provide cloud capabilities for data storage, management, and processing.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: AWS and Azure are best described as what?
options: Competing cloud platforms offering overlapping categories of services
questions.explanation: AWS and Azure are cloud platforms with services across compute, storage, networking, and more.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: Which statement best distinguishes EC2 from Lambda?
options: EC2 is object storage; Lambda is a Git host
Lambda requires a customer-managed VM for every invocation
EC2 provides virtual machines; Lambda runs functions in a managed event-driven environment
questions.explanation: EC2 provides VM instances, while Lambda abstracts server management for function execution.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: An EC2 instance has a public IP but cannot reach the internet. Which VPC elements may still need review?
options: Subnet route table, internet gateway attachment, and security rules
Git commit history and branch names
questions.explanation: Public internet access depends on routing, gateway configuration, addressing, and traffic rules.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: What is a practical reason to study big-data technologies on a cloud platform?
options: Cloud services can provide scalable compute and storage for data workloads
Big data eliminates the need for data governance
Cloud platforms do not require network configuration
questions.explanation: Cloud platforms can supply elastic resources for processing and storing large data workloads.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: How is data commonly addressed in S3?
options: As Linux processes identified by PID
As rows in an EC2 security group
questions.explanation: S3 stores objects in buckets and addresses them using object keys within a bucket.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: A database server should accept connections only from the application tier. Which configuration principle should be followed?
options: Open every port to all addresses
Place the database in a public subnet with no rules
Restrict network access to the required source and port
questions.explanation: Least-privilege network rules should permit only necessary sources and ports.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: Before launching an EC2 instance, which choice affects the operating system and initial software configuration?
questions.explanation: The chosen machine image determines the base operating system and may include preinstalled software.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: In the syllabus lab, why deploy an application on AWS using GitHub?
options: To make GitHub provide the EC2 CPU
To combine source control with a cloud runtime for the application
To turn every repository into an S3 bucket
To avoid configuring or testing the application
questions.explanation: GitHub stores and tracks source code, while AWS provides cloud resources on which the application can run.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 8–9 AWS and Azure
questions.question_text: Which AWS service in the syllabus is the clearest match for launching a Linux virtual machine?
questions.explanation: EC2 is the AWS compute service used to launch virtual machine instances.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: Which sequence contains stages named in the DevOps lifecycle overview?
options: Install, Print, Sort, Zip, Delete, Exit
Read, Write, Mount, Unmount, Fork, Wait
Create, Select, Group, Plot, Save, Quit
Plan, Code, Build, Test, Deploy, Monitor
questions.explanation: The syllabus lifecycle lists Plan, Code, Build, Test, Deploy, and Monitor.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: In the lifecycle overview, which stage commonly follows Build?
questions.explanation: The listed order proceeds from Build to Test, then Deploy and Monitor.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: Which statement best distinguishes DevOps from Agile?
options: Agile is a cloud vendor; DevOps is a Linux kernel
Agile focuses on iterative development; DevOps emphasizes collaboration across development and operations, including delivery and operation
questions.explanation: Agile and DevOps are related approaches; DevOps extends collaboration across software delivery and operations.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: What is the main idea of continuous integration (CI)?
options: Store code only on one developer's laptop
Integrate code changes frequently and validate them with automated builds or tests
questions.explanation: CI encourages frequent integration and automated validation to detect problems early.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: What is the goal of continuous delivery?
options: Replace Git with a Docker container
Keep software in a deployable state through an automated delivery process
questions.explanation: Continuous delivery automates build, test, and release preparation so changes can be deployed reliably.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: What is a CI/CD pipeline?
options: An automated sequence that builds, tests, and delivers software changes
A Linux command that lists processes
questions.explanation: A pipeline automates repeatable stages in integrating, validating, and delivering software.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: What is a Docker container?
options: A Git commit with a special name
A runnable isolated environment created from an image
questions.explanation: A container is a running instance of an image with an isolated application environment.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: What is a Docker image?
options: A packaged template used to create containers
questions.explanation: An image contains the filesystem and metadata from which containers are created.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: What is a Dockerfile?
options: A text file describing steps to build a Docker image
questions.explanation: A Dockerfile contains instructions used by Docker to build an image.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: Which Docker command builds an image from a Dockerfile in the current directory?
questions.explanation: docker build reads a build context and Dockerfile to create an image.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: Which Docker command creates and starts a container from an image?
questions.explanation: docker run creates a container from an image and starts it.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: Which command lists running Docker containers?
questions.explanation: docker ps displays running containers; an option can include stopped containers as well.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: What does docker stop app-container request?
options: Delete the image from a registry
Open a shell in every container
Stop the running container named app-container
questions.explanation: docker stop asks a running container to stop gracefully, then terminates it if needed.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: What does docker pull image-name do?
options: Download an image from a registry
Upload an image to a registry
questions.explanation: docker pull retrieves an image from a container registry.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: What does docker push image-name do?
options: Download an image from a registry
Upload an image to a registry
questions.explanation: docker push uploads a locally available image to a registry, subject to authentication and naming.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: What is docker exec commonly used for?
options: Push an image to Docker Hub
Run a command inside an already running container
questions.explanation: docker exec starts an additional process inside a running container.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: What is Docker Hub commonly used for?
questions.explanation: Docker Hub is a registry service for storing and sharing container images.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: A team changes its Dockerfile and wants a container to use that change. What must generally happen first?
options: Build a new image, then create or run a container from it
questions.explanation: Changes to the Dockerfile are incorporated by building a new image before running a container from it.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: In the syllabus lab, after building and running the ML application container, what should be tested?
questions.explanation: The lab asks students to run the container and test the ML API endpoint.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Session 10 Introduction to DevOps
questions.question_text: Why package an application and its dependencies into a container image?
options: To eliminate the need for application testing
To provide a consistent runtime package across compatible environments
questions.explanation: Container images package an application environment to improve consistency across deployment stages.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: A test environment is no longer needed after a deployment exercise. What can reduce unnecessary cloud resource use?
options: Create additional copies of every resource
Stop or release resources that are no longer required
questions.explanation: Releasing unused resources can reduce ongoing consumption and cost.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: Which metric is most directly useful for monitoring whether a deployed endpoint responds promptly?
questions.explanation: Latency measures response time and can reveal performance degradation.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: A deployment is marked complete, but the application returns errors. Which action is most appropriate?
options: Assume deployment success means the app is correct
Inspect application and service logs, configuration, and health metrics
questions.explanation: Logs, configuration, and health signals help locate deployment or runtime problems.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: A cloud application needs both a runtime to execute code and storage for uploaded files. What should the architecture include?
options: A load balancer without any application or data service
questions.explanation: An application needing execution and persistent files requires appropriate compute and storage capabilities.

questions.topic: Cloud Computing: Sessions 5–6 Cloud Services and Application Deployment
questions.question_text: Why should a team test an application after deployment in the cloud environment?
options: To prove that the application needs no monitoring
To verify that the deployed configuration and dependencies work in that environment
questions.explanation: Deployment testing verifies the application works with the actual cloud configuration and dependencies.
